title: Do women belong in the gym?
summary: NH analyses anti-women sentiment in online fitness and calls for male-only gyms. He attributes it mainly to male sexual frustration and resentment, criticises gym-positivity influencers who profit from it, and argues that serious female lifters deserve respect while men are responsible for controlling their gaze and libido.
claims: If women's gym clothes distract you, it is your responsibility to stop looking; controlling your gaze trains control of your libido
Resentment toward women in the gym stems mostly from sexual frustration, not their clothing
In 2020 one in three young men reported no sexual activity for the year; sexual inactivity rose from 18% to 31% between 2002 and 2018
The viral 'gym creep' videos were blown out of proportion by influencers such as Joey Swoll who profit from men's frustration
Masculinity gurus remove men's responsibility and blame outside factors, which keeps men frustrated and keeps the gurus relevant
Men need 'struggle tissue' (muscle earned through years of training and diet) to look good, while women's attractiveness depends mostly on bone structure and fat distribution
Women cannot build curves they were not born with by training; squats only slightly enlarge glutes and pressing does not enlarge breasts, whereas men with poor genetics can still transform
In years of training in gyms he has never had a problem with a woman; the offenders are almost always men, and women are often hit on repeatedly
Women in a male-dominated gym are often defensive because they are uncomfortable; a woman who refused to let him work in likely did not know what 'working in' meant
A 'gym positivity' movement is like body positivity: trying to change society instead of yourself
Male-only gyms already exist in practice: commercial weight rooms are ~90% men and hardcore gyms ~99% men
Female-only gyms rarely work because men pay most memberships, just as men make up 63-74% of women's soccer viewers
Female potential in sports is untapped because women feel unwelcome and almost all fitness content is made by men for men
Hypersexualized female fitness content exists because men reward it with clicks; men both drive and condemn it
Mocking serious female lifters as 'manly' is pathetic: men's size and strength advantage comes from 10x the testosterone and thicker bones
Women benefit greatly from weightlifting; supporting serious female lifters would also make gyms better
Making the gym 'inclusive' for normies degrades it (Planet Fitness); women who want to lift will adapt and mostly just want to be left alone
